name: FKA twigs
label: Young/Atlantic
lede: She started as the girl in the back of Jessie J's videos and ended up with a Grammy for a techno record she made after moving to Prague.

eras.title: The girl in the back of the video
eras.text: Tahliah Barnett came out of Cheltenham and the BRIT School as a dancer, working behind other people's hits while she figured out her own sound. By the end of 2012 she had a new name and a first EP on Bandcamp.

years.h: Backup dancing for Jessie J, Kylie Minogue and Ed Sheeran
years.p: Before she sang a note in public, Tahliah Barnett danced in videos for Kylie Minogue, Plan B, Ed Sheeran, Taio Cruz, Wretch 32 and Jessie J, including "Do It like a Dude" and "Price Tag".
years.xp:
Barnett grew up in Cheltenham, won a scholarship to St Edward's School, then went to the BRIT School in South London at 17 to study dance, and later studied fine art at Croydon College. Per Wikipedia, she also worked as a hostess in a strip club and sang at The Box Soho while she was getting started.

The video work paid, but the songs she was writing on the side were the point.

years.h: Twigs, then FKA twigs
years.p: She was nicknamed "Twigs" for her cracking joints; a twin-sister act called the Twigs asked her to change it, so she added "FKA".
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Barnett says FKA is just three letters, not an acronym.

years.h: EP1 goes up on Bandcamp, with a video for every song
years.p: EP1 was self-released, and she posted the individual music videos to YouTube one by one.

eras.title: Water Me
eras.text: Jesse Kanda's video for "Water Me" made her a name overnight, EP2 put her on Young Turks and LP1 made her a Mercury nominee. Arca and a flock of producers built a sound that was quiet, strange and very loud in its feelings.

years.h: The "Water Me" video: a face, tears and 16 million views
years.p: Directed by Jesse Kanda with twigs credited as co-director, the clip went viral on YouTube; Wikipedia says it has over sixteen million views.
years.xp:
The Guardian named her New Band of the Day that August. The video's slow, morphing close-up of her face did most of the introducing.

Kanda kept directing her videos, including "How's That" from the same EP.

years.h: EP2 · four songs, fifteen minutes, Young Turks
years.p: "How's That", "Papi Pacify", "Water Me" and "Ultraviolet", made with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]]. Pitchfork gave it 8 out of 10.
years.xp: Dummy named it Album of the Week, while The Line of Best Fit was cooler on it at 6 out of 10, per Wikipedia's reception box. It came out on Young Turks, the label that would release her first three records.

years.h: BBC Sound of 2014 nominee
years.p: She was a BBC Sound of 2014 nominee and was on Spotify's and Billboard's lists of acts to watch.

years.h: LP1 · Young Turks
years.p: Her first album was recorded over 2013-14 with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]], [[Clams Casino|772a0eb3-fe31-4a08-b583-690296f44900]], [[Paul Epworth|65380f7e-cb7a-4594-ae44-28ff55160746]], [[Devonte Hynes|68eb8831-4d0b-4a2b-9209-3ccade5117f0]], [[Emile Haynie|d6f3c7d7-3c95-4bf6-8647-0efeec36d704]] and [[Sampha|130c2184-14f2-4180-a216-04b5a333be57]]. Pitchfork gave it 8.8.
years.xp:
LP1 debuted at No. 16 in the UK and No. 30 on the Billboard 200, with first-week US sales of 10,370 copies, per Wikipedia. It was shortlisted for the Mercury Prize in September and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Recording Package.

Time and Clash both ranked it the best album of 2014. Singles: "Two Weeks" (June 24), "Pendulum" and "Video Girl" (October).

eras.title: Melissa, and a body that wouldn't cooperate
eras.text: With M3LL155X she directed a 16-minute film and turned the music into theater. Then came a long quiet stretch: a residency, a fibroid surgery, a feature on an ASAP Rocky record and ads she directed and starred in.

years.cap: FKA twigs at Laneway Festival, Sydney on 31 January 2015. · Wikimedia
years.h: Congregata: a live show at the Roundhouse before she had a new record
years.p: A theatrical performance staged at London's Roundhouse in Camden, months before M3LL155X.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it as a theatrical performance at the Roundhouse in February 2015.

years.h: M3LL155X · a record and a 16-minute film
years.p: Four songs with Boots, and a self-directed film with Michèle Lamy as an anglerfish. Pitchfork gave it 8.6.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the EP explores "Melissa," her name for her own female energy, which she describes as a creative force rather than an alter ego. Metacritic collected 12 reviews for an 89. The film drew two MTV Video Music Award nominations in 2016, for visual effects and choreography.

years.h: Fibroid surgery: "a fruit bowl of pain every day"
years.p: She had surgery for fibroid tumours in December 2017 and later described living with them that way, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: In 2020 she adopted a vegan diet after finding that animal products made the fibroid symptoms worse, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Magdalene
eras.text: Five years after LP1 she returned with a record that turned heartbreak and a rebuilt body into choral, distorted, sometimes operatic pop. Pitchfork gave it 9.4 and Best New Music.

years.h: "Cellophane": a pole, a clay floor, a voice that cracks
years.p: The video, directed by Andrew Thomas Huang, shows her climbing a pole to meet a creature with her face, then falling into an underworld and being covered in clay.
years.xp:
Pitchfork made it Best New Track and its best song of 2019; The Guardian ranked it No. 6. Critics singled out the vocal, which one described as cracking and groaning as if dragging more weight than it can bear.

Several publications linked the song to her ended engagement to Robert Pattinson; twigs herself has described the album as about how heartbreak could be so all-encompassing, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Magdalene · Young Turks
years.p: Recorded across 2016-2019 with [[Nicolas Jaar|06e99a1b-4020-4380-ab27-1a3e0c5e557c]] and a long list of producers, including [[Skrillex|ae002c5d-aac6-490b-a39a-30aa9e2edf2b]], [[Jack Antonoff|1155a7a9-a7b4-46ba-ba27-6b6c98be487e]], [[Daniel Lopatin|d5cd6528-3185-4f1b-a297-807b00b16f83]] and [[Koreless|ec0bfe7d-fc42-43c7-a2ea-dbf33a869ba3]]. Pitchfork gave it 9.4 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
Metacritic's score is 88 from 28 reviews. "Holy Terrain" features [[Future|48262e82-db9f-4a92-b650-dfef979b73ec]]; the singles were "Cellophane" (April 24), "Holy Terrain" (September 9), "Home with You" (October 7) and "Sad Day" (November 4), per Wikipedia.

It was No. 1 on the year-end lists of The A.V. Club, Clash, Now and Time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Shia LaBeouf · Wikipedia: FKA twigs
years.h: She sues Shia LaBeouf; it settles five years later
years.p: She filed in Los Angeles Superior Court alleging sexual battery, assault and emotional distress; LaBeouf denied the allegations.
years.xp: The two had met on the set of Honey Boy and dated from mid-2018 to mid-2019, per Wikipedia. According to reporting cited there, LaBeouf first said he was "abusive" and expressed remorse, then denied the allegations. The case was set for trial several times and settled in July 2025 on confidential terms. Caprisongs and Eusexua were both made and released while it was pending.

eras.title: Caprisongs
eras.text: She signed to Atlantic while keeping her Young imprint, and made a mixtape by phone: DMs, FaceTimes and friends leaving voice notes. Critics kept it near the tops of their lists.

years.h: Signs to Atlantic Records
years.p: Her first Atlantic release was "Tears in the Club", out December 16.

years.h: "Tears in the Club" with The Weeknd: the first Atlantic single
years.p: Directed by Amber Grace Johnson, the video has twigs dancing in a club and performing in a fish tank while [[The Weeknd|c8b03190-306c-4120-bb0b-6f2ebfc06ea9]] watches.
years.xp: Writers include Tahliah Barnett, Abel Tesfaye, Ali Tamposi, Henry Walter, Alejandra Ghersi and Pablo Diaz-Reixa; producers were [[Cirkut|0eb93ee5-2e6a-4ab4-a988-99c9139a664a]], [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]] and [[El Guincho|7e57d8a2-e6eb-48dd-8e50-ff7eaa412ccb]]. It peaked at No. 12 in New Zealand and No. 79 in Canada, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Caprisongs · Young/Atlantic
years.p: A mixtape with [[Pa Salieu|03100b87-7d27-4d56-b049-2007599656cc]], [[Daniel Caesar|b46e298d-d3a5-4695-a03e-63e8c523b23e]], [[Rema|720c46ba-a0e4-4b58-aee2-3bd70c70901f]], [[Jorja Smith|d62614aa-ef2c-44cd-8a7b-91292755a1d0]], [[Unknown T|a688dc7a-c743-4ec2-9355-c3dcdb30bf0e]], Dystopia, [[Shygirl|9385f1a7-8623-4d0c-b171-f1e6e87220c5]] and The Weeknd. Pitchfork gave it 7.8.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, Metacritic scores it 80 from 17 reviews; it peaked at No. 91 on the Billboard 200 and topped the US Top Dance Albums chart. El Guincho executive-produced alongside twigs, with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]], [[Mike Dean|73e36439-1e9a-4925-bf2c-1d7f7885fbb0]] and Cirkut on the boards.

Rolling Stone ranked it No. 8 of 2022, Slant No. 4 and Entertainment Weekly No. 3.

q: curated primarily through DMs and Facetimes
years.h: Made by phone: friends on the record, voice notes between songs
years.p: NPR's review singled out the voice messages from friends that sit between the songs.
years.xp: NPR described the mixtape as a first for her, made with El Guincho and pulling from synth-pop, dancehall, grime, neo-soul and ambient. The review reads the voice notes as the scaffolding for a record where she drops the guarded avatar.

years.h: NME gives her the Godlike Genius award
years.p: She performed "Meta Angel" and "Tears in the Club" at the 2022 BandLab NME Awards and took the Godlike Genius prize.

years.src: NPR: FKA twigs Tiny Desk · Wikipedia: FKA twigs
years.h: Tiny Desk (Home): "Killer" debuts in a church
years.p: She performed "home with you", "killer" and "cellophane" at London's St. Matthias Church with piano, double bass, violin and cello.
years.xp: NPR's framing had her performing amid "flames of offering" in a sermon on the perils of devotion. "Killer" had not been released; its video followed on July 20, directed by Yoann Lemoine with Aron Piper on a Portuguese beach, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Caprisongs · Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2022
years.h: Pitchfork ranks Caprisongs No. 24 of 2022
years.p: It placed 24th on Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2022, after a 7.8 review in January.
years.xp: The 7.8 score comes from Wikipedia's reception box for the album. The rank is on Pitchfork's published list; year-end lists aggregates the top 50.

eras.title: Eusexua
eras.text: She used the gap between records to perform in couture, argue with an ad regulator, testify to the Senate and move to Prague, where techno became the next record. It won her a Grammy.

years.h: Valentino show: "Unearth Her" with Koreless
years.p: She debuted "Unearth Her" at Valentino's Paris Fashion Week show; the producer was [[Koreless|ec0bfe7d-fc42-43c7-a2ea-dbf33a869ba3]].

years.h: 85 demos leak; she says no new music for a while
years.p: After the leak of 85 demo tracks, she announced a pause in releases.

years.h: A Calvin Klein ad gets banned, then un-banned
years.p: The UK Advertising Standards Authority banned a semi-nude ad in January and revoked the ban in March; twigs said she was proud of her physicality.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the ASA revoked the ban after a climbdown.

years.h: She testifies to the US Senate about AI and deepfakes
years.p: Barnett appeared before the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Intellectual Property on artificial intelligence and deepfakes.

years.h: Eusexua · Young/Atlantic
years.p: Made across 2022-24 with [[Koreless|ec0bfe7d-fc42-43c7-a2ea-dbf33a869ba3]] after she moved to Prague and fell into the city's techno scene. Pitchfork gave it 9.1.
years.xp: Twigs told British Vogue the word describes the sensation of being so euphoric you could transcend human form, per Wikipedia. Metacritic scores it 87 from 24 reviews. It was nominated for the Mercury Prize and lost to Sam Fender's People Watching.

years.h: "Deep but not sad": what she wanted a techno record to be
years.p: Her description of the sound she was after, per Wikipedia's article on the album.
years.xp: She has said the record keeps the spirit of techno without being techno in the strict sense. Rich Juzwiak's Pitchfork review compared it to Madonna's Ray of Light and called it a masterful pop-star moment.

years.h: Eusexua: Afterglow
years.p: A reissue on Young/Atlantic, with "Cheap Hotel" and "Predictable Girl" as singles. Pitchfork scored it 8.0.

years.h: Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album
years.p: Eusexua won at the 68th Annual Grammy Awards, per Wikipedia.
